title: Aggregating Totals with COUNT, SUM, and AVG
realWorldScenario: The CFO needs macro metrics on delivered orders: total order count, total gross revenue, and the average order value.
questionStatement: Write a query on the `orders` table to calculate `total_orders` (count of rows), `gross_revenue` (sum of total_amount), and `avg_order_value` (average of total_amount rounded to 2 decimals) for orders with status `DELIVERED`.
starterCode:
-- Aggregate delivered orders
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
  SUM(total_amount) AS gross_revenue,
  ROUND(AVG(total_amount), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM orders
WHERE status = 'DELIVERED';
hints: Use COUNT(*) to count all matching rows.
Use SUM(total_amount) for revenue and AVG(total_amount) for average value.

testCases.description: Verify aggregate metrics for delivered orders
